body.translated_text: These [<s>ku</s>, <s>gati</s>, and <s>prādi</s> words] obligatorily compound with a semantically related word. [Example:] <s>kutsitaḥ puruṣaḥ</s> — <s>kupuruṣaḥ</s> (a bad man).
[Sūtra:] '<s>ūry-ādi-cvi-ḍāc aś ca</s>' (VLk 953 = P 1.4.61)

body.text: ūryādayaścvyantā ḍājantāśca kriyāyoge gatisaṃjñāḥ syuḥ / ūrīkṛtya / śuklīkṛtya / paṭapaṭākṛtya / supuruṣaḥ //

children.translated_text: (<s>Vārttika</s>:) '<s>pra</s> and the other [prefixes compound] in the sense of <s>gata</s> (gone) and the like, with the first case (nominative).'
(<s>Vārttika</s>:) '<s>ati</s> and the others [compound] in the sense of <s>krānta</s> (surpassed) and the like, with the second case (accusative).'

body.translated_text: <s>Ūri</s> and the other [words], <s>cvi</s>-ending words, and <s>ḍāc</s>-ending words receive the designation <s>gati</s> when connected with an action. [Examples:] <s>ūrīkṛtya</s> (having accepted). <s>śuklīkṛtya</s> (having made white). <s>paṭapaṭākṛtya</s> (having made a pattering sound). <s>supuruṣaḥ</s> (a good man).
[Sūtra:] '<s>ekavibhakti cāpūrvanipāte</s>' (VLk 954 = P 1.2.44)

body.text: vigrahe yanniyatavibhaktikaṃ tadupasarjanasaṃjñaṃ syānna tu tasya pūrvanipātaḥ //
body.translated_text: That which has a fixed case-ending in the analytical paraphrase (<s>vigraha</s>) receives the designation <s>upasarjana</s> (subordinate member), but it is not placed first.
[Sūtra:] '<s>go-striyor upasarjanasya</s>' (VLk 955 = P 1.2.48)

body.text: upasarjanaṃ yo gośabdaḥ strīpratyayāntaṃ ca tadantasya prātipadikasya hrasvaḥ syāt / atimālaḥ /

children.translated_text: (<s>Vārttika</s>:) '<s>ava</s> and the others [compound] in the sense of <s>kruṣṭa</s> (called out) and the like, with the third case (instrumental).'
[Example:] <s>avakruṣṭaḥ kokilayā</s> — <s>avakokilaḥ</s> (one called out to by a cuckoo).
(<s>Vārttika</s>:) '<s>pari</s> and the others [compound] in the sense of <s>glāna</s> (exhausted) and the like, with the fourth case (dative).'
(<s>Vārttika</s>:) '<s>nir</s> and the others [compound] in the sense of <s>krānta</s> (gone out) and the like, with the fifth case (ablative).'

body.translated_text: When the word <s>go</s> (cow) is the <s>upasarjana</s>, or [a word] ending in a feminine suffix — the final [vowel] of the <s>prātipadika</s> (nominal stem) ending in such [a word] becomes short. [Example:] <s>atimālaḥ</s> (one who has surpassed the garland).
[Sūtra:] '<s>tatropapadaṃ saptamī-stham</s>' (VLk 956 = P 3.1.92)

body.text: saptamyante pade karmaṇītyādau vācyatvena sthitaṃ yatkumbhādi tadvācakaṃ padamupapadasaṃjñaṃ syāt //
body.translated_text: A word such as <s>kumbha</s> (pot) that stands in the locative in [the analytical expression] '<s>karmaṇi</s>' (in the action) etc. — being established as what is to be expressed — the word denoting it receives the designation <s>upapada</s> (co-occurring word).
[Sūtra:] '<s>upapadam atiṅ</s>' (VLk 957 = P 2.2.19)

body.text: upapadaṃ subantaṃ samarthena nityaṃ samasyate / atiṅantaścāyaṃ samāsaḥ / kumbham karoti kumbhakāraḥ / atiṅ kim ? mā bhavān bhūt / māṅi luṅiti saptamīnirdeśānmāṅupapadam / (pa.)

children.text: gatikārakopapadānāṃ kṛdbhiḥ saha samāsavacanaṃ prāk subutpatteḥ
children.translated_text: (<s>Vārttika</s>:) 'The compounding of <s>gati</s>, <s>kāraka</s>, and <s>upapada</s> with <s>kṛt</s> affixes should be stated as taking place before the assignment of case-endings.'
[Examples:] <s>vyāghrī</s> (tigress). <s>aśvakrītī</s> (one who buys horses). <s>kacchapī</s> (female tortoise), and so forth.

body.translated_text: The <s>upapada</s>, being a word ending in a case-ending, obligatorily compounds with a semantically related word. And this compound is non-verbal (<s>atiṅ</s>). [Example:] <s>kumbham karoti</s> — <s>kumbhakāraḥ</s> (pot-maker). Why <s>atiṅ</s> (non-verbal)? [Counter-example:] <s>mā bhavān bhūt</s> (may you not be!) — since the seventh case is used in [the sūtra] '<s>māṅi luṅi</s>', <s>māṅ</s> is the <s>upapada</s> [but no compound is formed with a finite verb].
[Sūtra:] '<s>tatpuruṣasyāṅguleḥ saṃkhyā-vyayādeḥ</s>' (VLk 958 = P 5.4.86)

body.text: saṃkhyāvyayāderaṅgulyantasya samāsānto 'c syāt / dve aṅgulī pramāṇamasya dvyaṅgulam / nirgatamaṅgulyo niraṅgulam //
body.translated_text: After a <s>tatpuruṣa</s> compound ending in <s>aṅguli</s> (finger/digit) that has a numeral or indeclinable as its prior member, the <s>ac</s> suffix is added as the final element of the compound. [Examples:] <s>dve aṅgulī pramāṇam asya</s> — <s>dvyaṅgulam</s> (two fingers in measure). <s>nirgatam aṅgulyaḥ</s> — <s>niraṅgulam</s> (without fingers).
[Sūtra:] '<s>ahaḥ-sarvaika-deśa-saṃkhyāta-puṇyāc ca rātreḥ</s>' (VLk 959 = P 5.4.87)

From these [words], after [a compound ending in] <s>rātri</s> (night), the <s>ac</s> [suffix] is added; and also after a numeral or indeclinable [as prior member]. The mention of <s>ahar</s> (day) is for the purpose of <s>dvandva</s> [compound formation].
[Sūtra:] '<s>rātrāhnāhāḥ puṃsi</s>' (VLk 960 = P 2.4.29)

body.text: etadantau dvandvatatpuruṣau puṃsyeva / ahaśca rātriścāhorātraḥ / sarvarātraḥ / saṃkhyātarātraḥ / (

children.translated_text: (<s>Vārttika</s>:) 'A <s>rātra</s> [compound] with a numeral as prior member is neuter.'
[Examples:] <s>dvirātram</s> (a period of two nights). <s>trirātram</s> (a period of three nights).

body.translated_text: Compounds ending in these [<s>rātra</s>, <s>ahna</s>, <s>āha</s>] are masculine only in <s>dvandva</s> and <s>tatpuruṣa</s>. [Examples:] <s>ahaś ca rātriś ca</s> — <s>ahorātraḥ</s> (a day-and-night). <s>sarvarātraḥ</s> (the whole night). <s>saṃkhyātarātraḥ</s> (a counted number of nights).
[Sūtra:] '<s>rājāhaḥ-sakhibhyaṣ ṭac</s>' (VLk 961 = P 5.4.91)
After a <s>tatpuruṣa</s> ending in these [<s>rājan</s>, <s>ahas</s>, <s>sakhi</s>], the <s>ṭac</s> [suffix] is added [as a compound-final element]. [Example:] <s>paramarājaḥ</s> (supreme king).
[Sūtra:] '<s>ān mahataḥ samānādhikaraṇa-jātīyayoḥ</s>' (VLk 962 = P 6.3.46)

body.text: mahata ākāro 'ntādeśaḥ syātsamānādhikaraṇe uttarapade jātīye ca pare / mahārājaḥ / prakāravacane jātīyar / mahāprakāro mahājātīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: For the word <s>mahat</s> (great), the final [vowel] is replaced by <s>ā</s> when a co-referential latter member or one meaning '<s>jātīya</s>' (of the kind) follows. [Example:] <s>mahārājaḥ</s> (great king). For the word <s>jātīya</s> denoting manner — <s>mahāprakāraḥ</s> [becomes] <s>mahājātīyaḥ</s> (of a great kind).
[Sūtra:] '<s>dvy-aṣṭanaḥ saṃkhyāyām abahuvrīhy-aśītyoḥ</s>' (VLk 963 = P 6.3.47)

body.text: ātsyāt / dvau ca daśa ca dvādaśa / aṣṭāviṃśatiḥ //
body.translated_text: [The final vowel becomes] <s>ā</s>. [Examples:] <s>dvau ca daśa ca</s> — <s>dvādaśa</s> (twelve). <s>aṣṭāviṃśatiḥ</s> (twenty-eight).
[Sūtra:] '<s>tres trayaḥ</s>' (VLk 964 = P 6.3.48)
[Examples:] <s>trayodaśa</s> (thirteen). <s>trayoviṃśatiḥ</s> (twenty-three). <s>trayastriṃśat</s> (thirty-three).
[Sūtra:] '<s>para-val-liṅgaṃ dvandva-tatpuruṣayoḥ</s>' (VLk 965 = P 2.4.26)

body.text: etayoḥ parapadasyeva liṅgaṃ syāt / kukkuṭamayūryāvime / mayūrīkukkuṭāvimau / (

children.translated_text: (<s>Vārttika</s>:) 'A prohibition should be stated for <s>dvigu</s>, <s>prāpta</s>, <s>āpanna</s>, <s>alam</s>, <s>pūrva</s>, and <s>gati</s> compounds.'

children.text: ḥ) / pañcasu kapāleṣu saṃskṛtaḥ pañcakapālaḥ puroḍāśaḥ //
children.translated_text: [Example:] <s>pañcasu kapāleṣu saṃskṛtaḥ</s> — <s>pañcakapālaḥ puroḍāśaḥ</s> (a sacrificial cake prepared in five potsherds).

body.translated_text: In these two [compound types, <s>dvandva</s> and <s>tatpuruṣa</s>], the gender of the latter member alone prevails. [Examples:] <s>kukkuṭamayūryau ime</s> (these are a rooster and a peahen [feminine]). <s>mayūrīkukkuṭau imau</s> (these are a peahen and a rooster [masculine]).
[Sūtra:] '<s>prāptāpanne ca dvitīyayā</s>' (VLk 966 = P 2.2.4)

body.text: samasyete / akāraścānayorantādeśaḥ / prāpto jīvikāṃ prāptajīvikaḥ / āpannajīvikaḥ / alaṃ kumāryai - alaṃkumāriḥ / ata eva jñāpakātsamāsaḥ / niṣkauśāmbiḥ //
body.translated_text: These [<s>prāpta</s> and <s>āpanna</s>] compound [with an accusative-ending word]. And the final replacement by <s>a</s> [applies] for these. [Examples:] <s>prāpto jīvikāṃ</s> — <s>prāptajīvikaḥ</s> (one who has obtained a livelihood). <s>āpannajīvikaḥ</s> (one who has attained a livelihood). <s>alaṃ kumāryai</s> — <s>alaṃkumāriḥ</s> (sufficient for the girl). By this very <s>jñāpaka</s> (indicatory device), the compound [is established]: <s>niṣkauśāmbiḥ</s> (one who has departed from <s>Kauśāmbī</s>).
[Sūtra:] '<s>ardharcāḥ puṃsi ca</s>' (VLk 967 = P 2.4.31)

body.text: ardharcādayaḥ śabdāḥ puṃsi klībe ca syuḥ / ardharcaḥ / ardharcam / evaṃ dhvajatīrthaśarīramaṇḍapayūpadehāṅkuśapātrasūtrādayaḥ / sāmānye napuṃsakam / mṛdu pacati / prātaḥ kamanīyam //
body.translated_text: The words <s>ardharca</s> (half-verse) and the others are [used] in masculine and neuter. [Examples:] <s>ardharcaḥ</s> (masculine). <s>ardharcam</s> (neuter). Similarly <s>dhvaja</s> (flag), <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred ford), <s>śarīra</s> (body), <s>maṇḍapa</s> (pavilion), <s>yūpa</s> (sacrificial post), <s>deha</s> (body), <s>aṅkuśa</s> (goad), <s>pātra</s> (vessel), <s>sūtra</s> (thread), and so forth. In the general [expression of a quality], the neuter [is used]. [Examples:] <s>mṛdu pacati</s> (he cooks softly). <s>prātaḥ kamanīyam</s> (the morning is lovely).
Thus [ends] the <s>tatpuruṣa</s> [compound]. (Section 3)
Now the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> [compound].
[Sūtra:] '<s>śeṣo bahuvrīhiḥ</s>' (VLk 968 = P 2.2.23)
This is a governing rule (<s>adhikāra</s>) extending up to [the section on] <s>dvandva</s>.
[Sūtra:] '<s>anekam anyapadārthe</s>' (VLk 969 = P 2.2.24)

body.text: anekaṃ prathamāntamanyasya padasyārthe vartamānaṃ vā samasyate sa bahuvrīhiḥ //
body.translated_text: Multiple words in the nominative case, denoting the meaning of another word, optionally compound — that is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s>.
[Sūtra:] '<s>saptamī-viśeṣaṇe bahuvrīhau</s>' (VLk 970 = P 2.2.35)

body.text: saptamyantaṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ ca bahuvrīhau pūrvaṃ syāt / ata eva jñāpakādvyadhikaraṇapado bahuvrīhiḥ //
body.translated_text: In a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound, a locative-ending word and a qualifier are placed first. By this very <s>jñāpaka</s> (indicatory device), it is established that a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> can have members in different case relations.
[Sūtra:] '<s>halantāt saptamyāḥ saṃjñāyām</s>' (VLk 971 = P 6.3.9)

body.text: halantādadantācca saptamyā aluk / kaṇṭhekālaḥ / prāptamudakaṃ yaṃ sa prāptodako grāmaḥ / ūḍharatho 'naḍvān / upahṛtapaśū rudraḥ / uddhṛtaudanā sthālī / pītāmbaro hariḥ / vīrapuruṣako grāmaḥ / (

children.translated_text: (<s>Vārttika</s>:) 'After <s>pra</s> and the other [prefixes], deletion of the latter member derived from a root should be optionally stated.'
(<s>Vārttika</s>:) 'After <s>nañ</s>, for [compounds with words] having the meaning of existence, deletion of the latter member should be optionally stated.'

body.translated_text: After a consonant-ending or <s>a</s>-ending [word], the locative case-ending is not deleted (<s>aluk</s>) [in a proper name]. [Examples:] <s>kaṇṭhekālaḥ</s> (one who has death at the throat). <s>prāptam udakaṃ yaṃ sa prāptodako grāmaḥ</s> (a village that has received water). <s>ūḍharatho 'naḍvān</s> (a bull whose cart has been taken away). <s>upahṛtapaśū Rudraḥ</s> (<s>Rudra</s> to whom animals have been offered). <s>uddhṛtaudanā sthālī</s> (a pot from which the rice has been removed). <s>pītāmbaro Hariḥ</s> (<s>Hari</s> who wears yellow garments). <s>vīrapuruṣako grāmaḥ</s> (a village having heroic men).
[Sūtra:] '<s>striyāḥ puṃvad bhāṣita-puṃskād anūṅ samānādhikaraṇe striyām apūraṇī-priyādiṣu</s>' (VLk 972 = P 6.3.34)

body.text: uktapuṃskādanūṅ ūṅo'bhāvo 'syāmiti bahuvrīhiḥ / nipātanātpañcamyā aluk ṣaṣṭhyāśca luk / tulye pravṛttinimitte yaduktapuṃskaṃ tasmātpara ūṅo'bhāvo yatra tathābhūtasya strīvācakaśabdasya puṃvācakasyeva rūpaṃ syāt samānādhikaraṇe strīliṅge uttarapade na tu pūraṇyāṃ priyādau ca parataḥ / gostriyoriti hrasvaḥ / citraguḥ / rūpavadbhāryaḥ / anūṅ kim ? vāmorūbhāryaḥ // pūraṇyāṃ tu - .
body.translated_text: This is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s>: '<s>anūṅ</s>' means 'that from which <s>ūṅ</s> is absent.' By <s>nipātana</s> (special stipulation), <s>aluk</s> applies for the fifth case and <s>luk</s> for the sixth case. When there is an equal basis for application — from a word designated as having a masculine form in ordinary usage (<s>bhāṣitapuṃska</s>), the absence of <s>ūṅ</s> being the case, the form of a feminine-denoting word takes the same form as the masculine-denoting word — when a co-referential feminine latter member follows, but not before a <s>pūraṇī</s> (ordinal) or <s>priya</s> and the like. By '<s>go-striyoḥ</s>' — shortening [applies]. [Examples:] <s>citraguḥ</s> (one with a variegated cow). <s>rūpavadbhāryaḥ</s> (one with a beautiful wife). Why <s>anūṅ</s>? [Counter-example:] <s>vāmorūbhāryaḥ</s> (one with a wife having beautiful thighs). Before a <s>pūraṇī</s> (ordinal), however —
[Sūtra:] '<s>ap-pūraṇī-pramāṇyoḥ</s>' (VLk 973 = P 5.4.116)

body.text: pūraṇārthapratyayāntaṃ yatstrīliṅgaṃ tadantātpramāṇyantācca bahuvrīhe rapsyāt / kalyāṇī pañcamī yāsāṃ rātrīṇāṃ tāḥ kalyāṇī pañcamā rātrayaḥ / strī pramāṇī yasya sa strīpramāṇaḥ / apriyādiṣu kim ? kalyāṇīpriya ityādi //
body.translated_text: After a word ending in a feminine ordinal (<s>pūraṇārtha</s>) suffix, and after one ending in <s>pramāṇī</s> — in a <s>bahuvrīhi</s>, the <s>ap</s> [suffix] is added. [Examples:] <s>kalyāṇī pañcamī yāsāṃ rātrīṇāṃ</s> — <s>tāḥ kalyāṇīpañcamā rātrayaḥ</s> (those nights whose fifth is auspicious). <s>strī pramāṇī yasya</s> — <s>sa strīpramāṇaḥ</s> (one whose standard is a woman). Why not before <s>priyādi</s>? [Answer:] <s>kalyāṇīpriya</s> and the like [retain the feminine form].
[Sūtra:] '<s>bahuvrīhau sakthy-akṣṇoḥ svāṅgāt ṣac</s>' (VLk 974 = P 5.4.113)

body.text: svāṅgavācisakthyakṣyantādbahuvrīheḥ ṣac syāt / dīrghasakthaḥ / jalajākṣī / svāṅgātkim ? dīrghasakthi śakaṭam / sthūlākṣā veṇuyaṣṭiḥ / akṣṇo 'darśanāditi vakṣyamāṇo 'c //
body.translated_text: After a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> ending in <s>sakthi</s> (thigh) or <s>akṣi</s> (eye), when the prior member denotes one's own body part, the <s>ṣac</s> suffix is added. [Examples:] <s>dīrghasakthaḥ</s> (long-thighed). <s>jalajākṣī</s> (lotus-eyed woman). Why 'one's own body part'? [Counter-examples:] <s>dīrghasakthi śakaṭam</s> (a cart with a long shaft). <s>sthūlākṣā veṇuyaṣṭiḥ</s> (a bamboo stick with thick knots). The <s>ac</s> suffix for <s>akṣan</s> will be stated [later] by the rule '<s>akṣṇo 'darśanāt</s>'.
[Sūtra:] '<s>dvi-tribhyāṃ ṣa mūrdhnaḥ</s>' (VLk 975 = P 5.4.115)

body.text: ābhyāṃ mūrdhnaḥ ṣaḥ syādbahuvrīhau / dvimūrdhaḥ / trimūrdhaḥ //
body.translated_text: After [<s>bahuvrīhi</s> compounds with] these two [numerals, <s>dvi</s> and <s>tri</s>] followed by <s>mūrdhan</s> (head), the <s>ṣa</s> suffix is added. [Examples:] <s>dvimūrdhaḥ</s> (two-headed). <s>trimūrdhaḥ</s> (three-headed).
[Sūtra:] '<s>antar-bahir-bhyāṃ ca lomnaḥ</s>' (VLk 976 = P 5.4.117)

After [<s>bahuvrīhi</s> compounds with] these two [<s>antar</s> and <s>bahir</s>] followed by <s>loman</s> (hair), the <s>ap</s> suffix is added. [Examples:] <s>antarlomaḥ</s> (having hair turned inward). <s>bahirlomaḥ</s> (having hair turned outward).
[Sūtra:] '<s>pādasya lopo 'hasty-ādibhyaḥ</s>' (VLk 977 = P 5.4.138)

body.text: hastyādivarjitādupamānātparasya pādaśabdasya lopaḥ syādbahuvrīhau / vyāghrasyeva pādāvasya vyāghrapāt / ahastyādibhyaḥ kim ? hastipādaḥ / kusūlapādaḥ //
body.translated_text: The word <s>pāda</s> (foot) is deleted in a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> after a word of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>), excluding <s>hasty-ādi</s> (words beginning with <s>hasti</s>). [Example:] <s>vyāghrasyeva pādāv asya</s> — <s>vyāghrapāt</s> (tiger-footed). Why 'excluding <s>hasty-ādi</s>'? [Counter-examples:] <s>hastipādaḥ</s> (elephant-footed). <s>kusūlapādaḥ</s> (granary-footed).
[Sūtra:] '<s>saṃkhyā-su-pūrvasya</s>' (VLk 978 = P 5.4.140)

body.text: pādasya lopaḥ syātsamāsānto bahuvrīhau / dvipāt / supāt //
body.translated_text: <s>Pāda</s> is deleted, and the compound-final [suffix is added], in a <s>bahuvrīhi</s>. [Examples:] <s>dvipāt</s> (two-footed). <s>supāt</s> (good-footed).
[Sūtra:] '<s>ud-vibhyāṃ kākudasya</s>' (VLk 979 = P 5.4.148)
[<s>Kākuda</s>] is deleted. [Examples:] <s>utkākut</s> (with raised hump). <s>vikākut</s> (with spreading hump).
[Sūtra:] '<s>pūrṇād vibhāṣā</s>' (VLk 980 = P 5.4.149)
<s>Pūrṇakākut</s> (full-crested — nom. sg.). <s>Pūrṇakākudaḥ</s> (gen. sg.).
<s>Suhṛd</s> and <s>durhṛd</s> [are used] for friend and enemy [respectively]. (VLk 981 = P 5.4.150)

body.text: sudurbhyāṃ hṛdayasya hṛdbhāvo nipātyate / suhṛnmitram / durhṛdamitraḥ //
body.translated_text: The shortening of <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart) to <s>hṛd</s> after <s>su</s> and <s>dur</s> is stipulated as an exception. <s>Suhṛt</s> means friend. <s>Durhṛt</s> means enemy.
From <s>uras</s> (chest) and the rest, [the suffix] <s>kap</s> [is added]. (VLk 982 = P 5.4.151)
When not at the beginning of a <s>pada</s>, [<s>visarga</s> becomes] <s>s</s>. (VLk 983 = P 8.3.38)
Before <s>pāśa</s>, <s>kalpaka</s>, and <s>kāmya</s>, <s>visarga</s> [becomes] <s>s</s>.
And in the <s>kaska</s>-group. (VLk 984 = P 8.3.48)

body.text: eṣviṇa uttarasya visargasya ṣo 'nyasya tu saḥ / iti saḥ / vyūḍhoraskaḥ //
body.translated_text: In these [words], the <s>visarga</s> following <s>iṇ</s> (vowels <s>i</s> and <s>u</s>) becomes <s>ṣ</s>; for others, [it becomes] <s>s</s>. Thus [the <s>visarga</s> becomes] <s>s</s>. <s>Vyūḍhoraskaḥ</s> (broad-chested).
After <s>iṇ</s> (vowels <s>i</s> and <s>u</s>), [<s>visarga</s> becomes] <s>ṣ</s>. (VLk 985 = P 8.3.39)

body.text: iṇa uttarasya visargasya ṣaḥ pāśakalpakakāmyeṣu pareṣu / priyasarpiṣkaḥ //
body.translated_text: The <s>visarga</s> following <s>iṇ</s> becomes <s>ṣ</s> before <s>pāśa</s>, <s>kalpaka</s>, and <s>kāmya</s>. <s>Priyasarpiṣkaḥ</s> (one fond of ghee).
A <s>niṣṭhā</s> (past participle) [in a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound is placed] first. (VLk 986 = P 2.2.36)
A <s>niṣṭhā</s>-final [member] should be placed first in a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound. <s>Yuktayogaḥ</s> (one connected with yoga).
From the remaining [types], optionally. (VLk 987 = P 5.4.154)
After a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> with a compound-final [member] not previously mentioned, <s>kap</s> [suffix is added] optionally. <s>Mahāyaśaskaḥ</s> or <s>mahāyaśāḥ</s> (of great fame).
Thus [ends] the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> [compound]. (4)
Now the <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound).
In the sense of <s>ca</s> (and), [it is called] <s>dvandva</s>. (VLk 988 = P 2.2.29)

body.text: anekaṃ subantaṃ cārthe vartamānaṃ vā samasyate sa dvandvaḥ / samuccayānvācayeta retarayogasamāhārāścārthāḥ / tatra "īśvaraṃ guruṃ ca bhajasva'; iti parasparanirapekṣasyāneka syaikasminnanvayaḥ samuccayaḥ / "bhikṣāmaṭa gāṃ cānaya'; ityanyatarasyānuṣaṅgikatvena anvayo 'nvācayaḥ / anayorasāmarthyātsamāso na / "dhavakhadirau chindhi'; iti militānāmanvaya itaretarayogaḥ / "saṃjñāparibhāṣam'; iti samūhaḥ samāhāraḥ //
body.translated_text: Multiple <s>sup</s>-ending [words] occurring in the sense of 'and' are optionally compounded — that is a <s>dvandva</s>. The senses of <s>ca</s> are: aggregation (<s>samuccaya</s>), sequential inclusion (<s>anvācaya</s>), mutual association (<s>itaretarayoga</s>), and collective unity (<s>samāhāra</s>). Among these, 'Worship the Lord and the teacher' — the association of multiple [objects], each independent of the other, in a single [predicate] is aggregation. 'Go for alms and bring a cow' — the association where one [action] is subsidiary to the other is sequential inclusion. For these two [types], compounding does not [occur] because of lack of semantic fitness. 'Cut the <s>dhava</s> and <s>khadira</s> [trees]' — the association of combined [objects] is mutual association. '<s>Saṃjñāparibhāṣam</s>' — a group is collective unity.
In the <s>rājadanta</s>-group, the [member denoting the] latter [in natural order is placed] last. (VLk 989 = P 2.2.31)

body.text: eṣu pūrvaprayogārhaṃ paraṃ syāt / dantānāṃ rājāno rājadantāḥ / (

children.translated_text: (In the <s>dharma</s>-group, there is no fixed rule
.) <s>Arthadharmau</s> (wealth and duty) or <s>dharmārthau</s> (duty and wealth) — and so forth.

body.translated_text: In these [compounds], the [member] worthy of prior mention is placed last. The kings of teeth — <s>rājadantāḥ</s> (the front teeth).
In a <s>dvandva</s>, a <s>ghi</s>-designated [word is placed] first. (VLk 990 = P 2.2.32)

body.text: dvandve ghisaṃjñaṃ pūrvaṃ syāt / hariśca haraśca hariharau //
body.translated_text: In a <s>dvandva</s>, a word designated <s>ghi</s> should be placed first. <s>Hari</s> and <s>Hara</s> — <s>Hariharau</s>.
A [word] beginning with a vowel and ending in <s>a</s> [is placed first]. (VLk 991 = P 2.2.33)
[Such a word] should be placed first in a <s>dvandva</s>. <s>Īśakṛṣṇau</s> (<s>Īśa</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>).
One with fewer syllables (<s>ac</s>) [is placed first]. (VLk 992 = P 2.2.34)
<s>Śivakeśavau</s> (<s>Śiva</s> and <s>Keśava</s>).
'Father' [may be placed before] 'mother.' (VLk 993 = P 1.2.70)

body.text: mātrā sahoktau pitā vā śiṣyate / mātā ca pitā ca pitarau, mātāpitarau vā //
body.translated_text: When mentioned together with 'mother,' 'father' is optionally [placed before it]. Mother and father — <s>pitarau</s>, or <s>mātāpitarau</s>.
And the <s>dvandva</s> of animate beings, musical instruments, and parts of an army [is treated as a singular collective]. (VLk 994 = P 2.4.2)

body.text: eṣāṃ dvandva ekavat / pāṇipādam / mārdaṅgikavaiṇavikam / rathikāśvāroham //
body.translated_text: The <s>dvandva</s> of these is [treated] as a single unit. <s>Pāṇipādam</s> (hands and feet). <s>Mārdaṅgikavaiṇavikam</s> (a drum-player and flute-player [pair]). <s>Rathikāśvāroham</s> (charioteers and horsemen).
From a <s>dvandva</s> ending in a <s>cu</s>-series consonant or in <s>ḍaṣah</s>, [the suffix] <s>ṭac</s> [is added] in the collective sense. (VLk 995 = P 5.4.106)

body.text: cavargāntāddaṣahāntācca dvandvāṭṭac syātsamāhāre / vāk ca tvak ca vāktvacam / tvaksrajam / śamīdṛṣadam / vāktviṣam / chatropānaham / samāhāre kim ? prāvṛṭśaradau //
body.translated_text: After a <s>dvandva</s> ending in a palatal (<s>cavarga</s>) or in <s>ḍaṣah</s>, [the suffix] <s>ṭac</s> [is added] in the collective sense (<s>samāhāra</s>). Speech and skin — <s>vāktvacam</s>. <s>Tvaksrajam</s>. <s>Śamīdṛṣadam</s>. <s>Vāktviṣam</s>. <s>Chatropānaham</s>. Why [the restriction to] the collective sense? <s>Prāvṛṭśaradau</s> (the rainy season and autumn [as separate items]).
Thus [ends] the <s>dvandva</s>. (5)
Now the <s>samāsānta</s> (compound-final) suffixes.
For [compounds ending in] <s>ṛc</s>, <s>pūr</s>, <s>ap</s>, <s>dhūḥ</s>, and <s>path</s>, <s>a</s> [is the compound-final suffix], not [before the word] <s>akṣa</s>. (VLk 996 = P 5.4.74)

body.text: a anakṣe iticchedaḥ / ṛgādyantasya samāsasya apratyayo 'ntāvayavo 'kṣe yā dhūstadantasya tu na / ardharcaḥ / viṣṇupuram / vimalāpaṃ saraḥ / rājadhurā / akṣe tu akṣadhūḥ / dṛḍhadhūrakṣaḥ / sakhipathaḥ / ramyapatho deśaḥ //
body.translated_text: The analysis is: <s>a</s>, <s>anakṣe</s>. For a compound ending in <s>ṛc</s> and the rest, [the compound-final] <s>a</s> suffix [is added] — a non-suffix final element — but not for [a compound ending in] <s>dhūḥ</s> before <s>akṣa</s>. <s>Ardharcaḥ</s> (a half-verse). <s>Viṣṇupuram</s> (city of <s>Viṣṇu</s>). <s>Vimalāpaṃ saraḥ</s> (a lake of clear water). <s>Rājadhurā</s> (royal burden). But before <s>akṣa</s>: <s>akṣadhūḥ</s>. <s>Dṛḍhadhūrakṣaḥ</s>. <s>Sakhipathaḥ</s> (friend's path). <s>Ramyapatho deśaḥ</s> (a region with pleasant paths).
For <s>akṣi</s> (eye), when not [denoting] seeing. (VLk 997 = P 5.4.76)
For <s>akṣi</s> (eye) that is not a synonym of <s>cakṣus</s> (sight), <s>ac</s> [suffix] is the compound-final. 'Like the eyes of cows — <s>gavākṣaḥ</s>' (window).
After an <s>upasarga</s>, for <s>adhvan</s> (road). (VLk 998 = P 5.4.85)
One who has gone far on the road — <s>prādhvo rathaḥ</s> (a chariot that has traveled far).
Not after [a word used in the sense of] honor. (VLk 999 = P 5.4.69)

body.text: pūjanārthātparebhyaḥ samāsāntā na syuḥ / surājā / atirājā //
body.translated_text: After [words] having the sense of honor, compound-final suffixes should not apply. <s>Surājā</s> (a good king). <s>Atirājā</s> (a supreme king).
Thus [end] the compound-final suffixes.
Now the <s>taddhita</s> (secondary derivational suffixes). First, the common suffixes.
Of [words that are] semantically connected, [the suffix is added] optionally after the first [case-form]. (VLk 1000 = P 4.1.82)
These three words are taken as the governing rules — up to '<s>prāgdiśa</s>' [i.e., throughout this section].
And from the <s>aśvapati</s>-group [the suffix <s>aṇ</s> is added]. (VLk 1001 = P 4.1.84)
From these, <s>aṇ</s> [is added] in the senses [ranging] up to '<s>dīvyati</s>' (to play/gamble). The offspring of <s>Aśvapati</s> and the like — <s>āśvapatam</s>. <s>Gāṇapatam</s>.
From <s>diti</s>, <s>aditi</s>, <s>āditya</s>, <s>apatya</s>, and words with <s>uttarapada</s> (final member) — <s>ṇya</s> [is added]. (VLk 1002 = P 7.2.117)

body.text: dityādibhyaḥ patyutatarapadācca prāgdīvyatiyeṣvartheṣu ṇyaḥ syāt / aṇo 'pavādaḥ / diterapatyaṃ daityaḥ / aditerādityasya vā //
body.translated_text: From <s>diti</s> and the rest, and from words with <s>pati</s> as their final member, <s>ṇya</s> [is added] in the senses up to '<s>dīvyati</s>.' This overrides <s>aṇ</s>. The offspring of <s>Diti</s> — <s>daityaḥ</s>. Or of <s>Aditi</s> — <s>ādityasya</s>.

body.text: halo yamāṃ yami lopaḥ // VLk_1003 = P_4,1.85 //
body.translated_text: Of <s>yam</s> (a doubled consonant after <s>hal</s>), [there is optional] elision before <s>yam</s>. (VLk 1003 = P 4.1.85)

body.text: halaḥ parasya yamo lopaḥ syād vā yami / iti yalopaḥ / ādityaḥ / prājāpatyaḥ / (
body.translated_text: A doubled consonant (<s>yam</s>) following a consonant (<s>hal</s>) optionally undergoes elision before [another] <s>yam</s>. Thus the <s>ya</s> undergoes elision. <s>Ādityaḥ</s>. <s>Prājāpatyaḥ</s>.
And before a <s>kit</s> [suffix]. (VLk 1004 = P 7.2.118)

body.text: kiti taddhite cācāmāderaco vṛddhiḥ syāt / vāhīkaḥ / (

children.translated_text: ). The offspring and the rest of a cow — <s>gavyam</s>.

body.translated_text: Before a <s>kit</s> <s>taddhita</s> suffix also, <s>vṛddhi</s> of the initial vowel applies. <s>Vāhīkaḥ</s>.
From the <s>utsa</s>-group, <s>añ</s> [is added]. (VLk 1005 = P 4.1.86)
<s>Autsaḥ</s>.
Thus [end] the common suffixes applicable to offspring, modification, and related meanings. (1)
Now the section on offspring (<s>apatya</s>).
From [words denoting] woman and man, <s>nañ</s> and <s>snañ</s> [are added respectively] in the sense of 'born from.' (VLk 1006 = P 4.1.87)

body.text: dhānyānāṃ bhavana ityataḥ prāgartheṣu strīpuṃsābhyāṃ kramānnañsnañau staḥ / straiṇaḥ / paiṃsnaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the senses [ranging] up to 'born from grain,' from [words denoting] woman and man, <s>nañ</s> and <s>snañ</s> [are added] respectively. <s>Straiṇaḥ</s> (born of a woman). <s>Paiṃsnaḥ</s> (born of a man).
'His offspring.' (VLk 1007 = P 4.1.92)

body.text: ṣaṣṭhyantātkṛtasandheḥ samarthādapatyer'the uktā vakṣyamāṇāśca pratyayā vā syuḥ //
body.translated_text: After a semantically connected [word] in the genitive, with <s>sandhi</s> applied, the suffixes stated [already] and those to be stated [below] are optionally [added] in the sense of offspring.
For [a stem ending in] <s>u</s>, <s>guṇa</s> [applies in the <s>bha</s>-stem]. (VLk 1008 = P 6.4.146)

body.text: uvarṇāntasya bhasya guṇastaddhite / upagorapatyamaupagavaḥ / āśvapataḥ / daityaḥ / autsaḥ / straiṇaḥ / paiṃsnaḥ //
body.translated_text: For the <s>bha</s>-stem ending in a <s>u</s>-vowel, <s>guṇa</s> [applies] before a <s>taddhita</s> [suffix]. The offspring of <s>Upagu</s> — <s>aupagavaḥ</s>. <s>Āśvapataḥ</s>. <s>Daityaḥ</s>. <s>Autsaḥ</s>. <s>Straiṇaḥ</s>. <s>Paiṃsnaḥ</s>.
Offspring from the grandson onward is [called] <s>gotra</s> (lineage name). (VLk 1009 = P 4.1.162)
Offspring intended as [belonging to the line] from the grandson onward is designated <s>gotra</s>.
Only one [suffix is applied] in [forming] a <s>gotra</s> [name]. (VLk 1010 = P 4.1.93)
In the <s>gotra</s> [formation], only one offspring-suffix is [applied]. The <s>gotra</s>-offspring of <s>Upagu</s> — <s>aupagavaḥ</s>.
From the <s>Garga</s>-group, <s>yañ</s> [is added]. (VLk 1011 = P 4.1.105)
In the <s>gotra</s>-offspring [formation]. The <s>gotra</s>-offspring of <s>Garga</s> — <s>gārgyaḥ</s>. <s>Vātsyaḥ</s>.
And [the suffixes] <s>yañ</s> and <s>añ</s> [undergo <s>luk</s> elision]. (VLk 1012 = P 2.4.64)

body.text: gotre yadyañantamañantaṃ ca tadavayavayoretayorluk syāttatkṛte bahutve na tu striyām / gargāḥ / vatsāḥ //
body.translated_text: In the <s>gotra</s> [formation], a <s>yañ</s>-final or <s>añ</s>-final [stem] — of its component parts, <s>luk</s> elision of these two [suffixes] applies when [the word denotes] plurality made by that [gotra suffix], but not in the feminine. <s>Gargāḥ</s> (the descendants of <s>Garga</s>). <s>Vatsāḥ</s>.

body.text: jīvati tu vaṃśye yuvā // VLk_1013 = P_4,1.163 //
body.translated_text: But while the ancestor is living, [the descendant is called] <s>yuvan</s> (young). (VLk 1013 = P 4.1.163)

body.text: vaṃśye pitrādau jīvati pautrāderyadapatyaṃ caturthādi tadyuvasaṃjñameva syāt //
body.translated_text: When the ancestor in the lineage — father or the like — is still living, the offspring from the grandson (fourth generation onward) is designated <s>yuvan</s> only.
From the <s>gotra</s> [stem], [a suffix is added] for the young offspring; but not [the <s>yuvan</s> designation] in the feminine. (VLk 1014 = P 4.1.94)

body.text: yūnyapatye gotrapratyayāntādeva pratyayaḥ syāt, striyāṃ tu na yuvasaṃjñā //
body.translated_text: The suffix for the young offspring is [added] from the <s>gotra</s>-suffix-final [stem] itself; but in the feminine, the <s>yuvan</s> designation does not [apply].
And from [stems ending in] <s>yañ</s> and <s>iñ</s> [the yuvan suffix is <s>phak</s>]. (VLk 1015 = P 4.1.101)
In the <s>gotra</s> [formation], from a stem ending in <s>yañ</s> or <s>iñ</s>, [the suffix] <s>phak</s> is [added for the yuvan].

For the initial sounds of the suffixes <s>pha</s>, <s>ḍha</s>, <s>kha</s>, <s>cha</s>, <s>gha</s> — [the substitutes are] <s>āyan</s>, <s>ey</s>, <s>īn</s>, <s>īy</s>, <s>iy</s> [respectively]. (VLk 1016 = P 7.1.2)

body.text: pratyayādeḥ phasya āyan, ḍhasya ey, khasya īn, chasya īy, ghasya iy ete syuḥ/ gargasya yuvāpatyaṃ gārgyāyaṇaḥ / dākṣāyaṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: The initial <s>pha</s> of a suffix [becomes] <s>āyan</s>; <s>ḍha</s> [becomes] <s>ey</s>; <s>kha</s> [becomes] <s>īn</s>; <s>cha</s> [becomes] <s>īy</s>; <s>gha</s> [becomes] <s>iy</s>. The <s>yuvan</s>-offspring of <s>Garga</s> — <s>gārgyāyaṇaḥ</s>. <s>Dākṣāyaṇaḥ</s>.
After [a stem ending in] <s>a</s>, <s>iñ</s> [is added]. (VLk 1017 = P 4.1.95)
In the sense of offspring. <s>Dākṣiḥ</s>.
And from the <s>bāhu</s>-group. (VLk 1018 = P 4.1.96)

children.translated_text: (For <s>loman</s>, in the plural offspring, the non-appearance of <s>a</s> is to be stated

body.translated_text: <s>Bāhaviḥ</s>. <s>Auḍulomiḥ</s>.
From the <s>bida</s>-group, <s>añ</s> [is added] for non-sages as indirect descendants. (VLk 1019 = P 4.1.104)

body.text: ebhyo 'ñ gotre / ye tvatrānṛṣayastebhyo 'patye 'nyatra tu gotre / bidasya gotraṃ baidaḥ / baidau / bidāḥ / putrasyāpatyaṃ pautraḥ / pautrau / pautrāḥ / evaṃ dauhitrādayaḥ //
body.translated_text: From these, <s>añ</s> [is added] in the <s>gotra</s> [formation]. But those among them who are non-sages — from them [<s>añ</s> is added] in the offspring sense, but elsewhere in the <s>gotra</s> [sense]. The <s>gotra</s> of <s>Bida</s> — <s>baidaḥ</s>. <s>Baidau</s>. <s>Bidāḥ</s>. The offspring of a son — <s>pautraḥ</s> (grandson). <s>Pautrau</s>. <s>Pautrāḥ</s>. Similarly <s>dauhitra</s> (daughter's son) and the rest.
From the <s>śiva</s>-group, <s>aṇ</s> [is added]. (VLk 1020 = P 4.1.112)
In the sense of offspring. <s>Śaivaḥ</s>. <s>Gāṅgaḥ</s>.
And from <s>ṛṣi</s>, <s>andhaka</s>, <s>vṛṣṇi</s>, <s>kuru</s>. (VLk 1021 = P 4.1.114)

body.text: ṛṣibhyaḥ - vāsiṣṭhaḥ / vaiśvāmitraḥ / andhakebhyaḥ - śvāphalkaḥ / vṛṣṇibhyaḥ - vāsudevaḥ / kurubhyaḥ - nākulaḥ / sāhadevaḥ //
body.translated_text: From sages: <s>vāsiṣṭhaḥ</s> (descendant of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>). <s>Vaiśvāmitraḥ</s>. From the <s>Andhakas</s>: <s>śvāphalkaḥ</s>. From the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>: <s>vāsudevaḥ</s>. From the <s>Kurus</s>: <s>nākulaḥ</s>. <s>Sāhadevaḥ</s>.
For <s>mātṛ</s> (mother), when preceded by a numeral, <s>saṃbhadra</s>, or [similar words]. (VLk 1022 = P 4.1.115)

body.text: saṃkhyādipūrvasya mātṛśabdasyodādeśaḥ syādaṇ pratyayaśca / dvaimāturaḥ / ṣāṇmāturaḥ / sāṃmāturaḥ / bhādramāturaḥ //
body.translated_text: The word <s>mātṛ</s> preceded by a numeral or the like receives the substitute <s>ud</s>, and the suffix <s>aṇ</s> [is added]. <s>Dvaimāturaḥ</s> (having two mothers). <s>Ṣāṇmāturaḥ</s>. <s>Sāṃmāturaḥ</s>. <s>Bhādramāturaḥ</s>.
From [stems ending in] feminine suffixes, <s>ḍhak</s> [is added]. (VLk 1023 = P 4.1.120)
From [stems] ending in a feminine suffix, <s>ḍhak</s> [is added]. <s>Vainateyaḥ</s> (son of <s>Vinatā</s>).
From <s>kanyā</s> (maiden), <s>kanīna</s> [is formed] as well. (VLk 1024 = P 4.1.116)
And by [the word <s>ca</s>], <s>aṇ</s> [is also added]. <s>Kānīnaḥ</s> — [such were] <s>Vyāsa</s> and <s>Karṇa</s> (sons of unmarried women).
From <s>rājan</s> (king) and <s>śvaśura</s> (father-in-law), <s>yat</s> [is added]. (VLk 1025 = P 4.1.137)

children.translated_text: (It is to be stated that [<s>yat</s> applies for <s>rājan</s>] only in the sense of birth [i.e., caste]

body.translated_text: And [a stem ending in <s>an</s>] before <s>ya</s>-initial [suffixes] retains its form, except in the <s>bhāva</s> and <s>karma</s> [senses]. (VLk 1026 = P 6.4.168)

body.text: yādau taddhite pare 'n prakṛtyā syānna tu bhāvakarmaṇoḥ / rājanyaḥ / jātāveveti kim ? - .
body.translated_text: Before a <s>ya</s>-initial <s>taddhita</s> suffix, [the stem ending in <s>an</s>] retains its form (<s>prakṛti</s>), but not in the <s>bhāva</s> and <s>karma</s> [senses]. <s>Rājanyaḥ</s> (of royal birth, <s>kṣatriya</s>). Why [the restriction to] 'birth only'?
<s>An</s> [stem retains its form]. (VLk 1027 = P 6.4.167)

body.text: an prakṛtyā syādaṇi pare / rājanaḥ / śvaśuryaḥ //
body.translated_text: An [<s>an</s>-final stem] retains its form before <s>aṇ</s>. <s>Rājanaḥ</s>. <s>Śvaśuryaḥ</s>.
From <s>kṣattṛ</s> (usher/mixed-caste person), <s>gha</s> [is added]. (VLk 1028 = P 4.1.138)
